correctness.rationale: A published structural fact states that every binary completely reachable automaton has a full-cycle letter. Fixing that letter to q->q+1 mod n is therefore exhaustive for the full binary class. The census checks every one of the n^n choices of the second map for each 2<=n<=8. Exact power-automaton BFS finds zero Don violations through n=7 and exactly 544 at n=8; every violation is one six-state subset at distance 17. The displayed representative is independently replayed, reaches all 255 nonempty subsets, and has exact target distance 17.

evidence: Zhu's Example 14 is a circular binary family stated for even n>=10, and Lemma 17 gives the lower bound 5n/2-3 for a subset of size n-2.

value.rationale: The published binary counterexample family begins at ten states, while current literature still treats that family as the relevant lower-bound mechanism. Because every binary completely reachable automaton has a full-cycle letter, the exhaustive normalized census settles the actual binary onset: eight states are possible and seven are impossible. The complete first-layer classification is stronger than an isolated witness.
